prose: NOT APPLICABLE IS THIS ROW'S KIND, NOT ITS VERDICT: AC-01.3 is a non-test criterion, so its row carries prose rather than a red-then-green, and the criterion is LIVE. Read its state from ac list, never from this row's n/a. THE EVIDENCE IS COMPLETE: all TEN arms are mutation-proven. EVERY ARM IS REDDENED BY AT LEAST ONE LANDED MUTATION, which is not one mutation per arm: M2 reddened arms 2, 3 and 4 together, A0 reddened eight, and A1 reddened exactly one. Those are all correct results about different arms, and the two extremes are what show the suite has resolution and not merely coverage: a mutation reddening exactly one arm says that arm is pinned to that behaviour and nothing else, while arm 0's cascade is right for what arm 0 is. Each mutation was applied ALONE to a FRESH COPY of opt/arngz/lib under the runner's scratchpad, so the tree's engine was never written, and each was PROVEN TO HAVE LANDED on exactly one line BEFORE being run, because a mutation that silently failed to apply would leave its arm passing and read as "this arm cannot go red", which is the opposite conclusion. PASS 1, slot YYCYT8, the four arms with a recorded defect behind them: the final-failure path not consulting made (arm 3, line 442, bf6e5f08); the creating call retried on a lagging count (arms 2, 3 and 4 together, line 393, fa0a7b58, the fix that was worse than what it replaced); the overshoot going unreported (arm 4, line 399); the vanished display retried instead of stopped (arm 6, line 419). PASS 2, slot CQXAX4, the six with NO defect history, which is why they were the ones most likely to be asserting nothing: is_user_space's accepted string (arm 0, plan.lua:287, eight arms red); the success readback off by one (arm 1, line 398, one arm red); the retry budget cut to one (arm 5, line 392); the count-before guard disabled (arm 7, line 362); the already-failed guard disabled (arm 8, line 357); the per-display lookup made global (arm 9, line 356). ARM 8 WAS THE POINT OF PASS 2 and it is not vacuous: it asserts that a display already bound is refused rather than retried, had nothing in its history to suggest it worked, and went red. ARM 7's MUTANT RAISED A REAL LUA ERROR, "bad argument #3 to 'format'", which M.execute's pcall converted into a reported failure the arm could tell apart from a genuine one: IN-AG-NO-SILENT-001 paying for itself under a test nobody wrote for it, and the first thing to exercise that pcall. BOTH ENGINE FILES ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL EITHER SIDE OF EVERY PASS: arngz.lua ad05df4fc50c0b0f37e71cde71e1062022c66a925b32b37b09419ef25d5e9c0e and plan.lua 465276e0c270195824d138b7e44eeef7a502354c9bac98b91c794f372d925714, with git status on opt/arngz/lib empty and no diff against 5d7bfe37, the arms' own head, so proving the driver cannot have disturbed their green. utilz-vc verified both hashes independently, and plan.lua's value was independently pinned from the other side of the tree by vc's own booking PDY9E2 minutes earlier, two nodes hashing one file for different reasons and agreeing. THE PER-MUTANT COUNTS, transcribed from each run's own summary line so the parse question stays closed for a reader who was not there. The driver's first act is dofile on the engine, so a mutant that failed to parse would have raised before printing a single ok and produced no summary at all; every one of the ten printed a summary with most arms passing, so each loaded and executed, which is stronger evidence than luac -p. Control, YYCYT8: 45 passed, 0 failed. Pass 1, YYCYT8: M1 44 passed 1 failed; M2 42 passed 3 failed; M3 44 passed 1 failed; M4 43 passed 2 failed. Pass 2, CQXAX4, which ran the six mutants and NO control: A0 37 passed 8 failed; A1 44 passed 1 failed; A5 39 passed 6 failed; A7 42 passed 3 failed, its red raised at runtime and converted by pcall with 42 passing around it; A8 43 passed 2 failed; A9 42 passed 3 failed. In every run passed plus failed is the driver's whole set, so no mutant crashed partway and dropped checks.
